title: Zeabur unauthorized access to project environment-variable data
confirmed_facts: Zeabur reported that a leaked internal AWS administrative credential was used to access its shared Tokyo AWS cluster.
Zeabur reported subsequent VPN access to its control-plane network and access to its primary database.
Zeabur identified targeted queries and exports involving customer environment variables and reported that directly usable AI and other service credentials appeared to be targeted.
Zeabur revoked and rotated known affected credentials while a third-party forensic investigation remained in progress.
inferences: The public update supports reviewing secret bulk-read boundaries, cloud IAM lateral movement, and rotation blast radius; it does not yet establish the complete root cause or full data-access scope.
No assertion is made here that a specific ContextSec control was absent in Zeabur's implementation.
failure_patterns: downstream credential cascade and rotation burden
trust_boundaries: AWS administrative identity to shared cluster
control_hypotheses: A secret platform needs a first-class bulk-access invariant in addition to ordinary at-rest encryption.
Credential containment must model transitive authority from cloud IAM through internal networks to customer secret stores.
Incident regression should verify both revocation of the entry credential and cascade rotation of downstream credentials.

regression.mutation: Introduce a batch secret export with no tenant/workload predicate or volume ceiling and require SECRET-BULK-001 to fail.
